title: Left inverses of a matrix up to a scalar and its maximal minors
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge m\ge0$ integers, $A$ an $n\times m$ matrix with entries in $R$, and $J\subseteq R$ the ideal generated by the $m\times m$ minors of $A$, i.e. by the determinants $\det(A_I)$, $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$, $|I|=m$, where $A_I$ is the $m\times m$ matrix formed by the rows of $A$ with indices in $I$ (for $m=0$, $J=R$, the empty minor being $1$). (1) For every $f\in J$ there is an $m\times n$ matrix $B$ over $R$ with $BA=f\cdot1_{m\times m}$. (2) If $f\in R$ and $B$ is an $m\times n$ matrix over $R$ with $BA=f\cdot1_{m\times m}$, then $f^m\in J$; explicitly $f^m=\sum_{|I|=m}b_I\det(A_I)$ with $b_I$ the determinant of the $m\times m$ matrix formed by the columns of $B$ with indices in $I$ (Cauchy–Binet).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse, line 2668) and its proof (adjugates of the A_I for (1); the Cauchy-Binet formula, item-cauchy-binet, for (2)); used for Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07ET (lemma-parse-equation-strictly-standard-one)
